title: Premature Optimization
pattern: Writing complex, non-obvious, or unsafe code for hypothetical performance gains during initial drafting, without any profiling or benchmark data.
why_bad: It sacrifices clarity, readability, and correct architecture for unverified performance benefits. Programs spend 90% of their time in 10% of the code; optimizing non-hot-paths adds maintenance hazards and bypasses compiler optimizations without real gains.
detection: Usage of `unsafe` blocks, manual pointer manipulations, complex manual loop unrolling, or custom caching mechanisms in non-hot paths with no associated performance tests or profiling data.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level library components (like core database indexing or high-frequency renderers) with strict, predefined performance constraints backed by benchmark suites.
fix: Write the code in the simplest, most readable, and idiomatic way first. Benchmark and profile later, and optimize only the proven bottlenecks.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 25 ("Code-Tuning Strategies - Premature Optimization"), p. 597; Martin Fowler et al., *Refactoring*, Section on Performance, p. 70.
